purpose.HookemonHook.sol: Concrete, deployable Uniswap v4 hook contract for the HKMN/USDG canonical pool. Composes HolderSettlement + CanonicalMarketCallback + HookemonIssuance via multiple inheritance, wires the abstract FeeAccounting/CanonicalMarketCallback hooks to concrete USDG token calls (raw staticcall/call, fail-closed), enforces the CREATE2-mined hook permission mask (0x00CC) at construction, and exposes external swap callbacks plus liability read/claim entry points.
purpose.CanonicalMarket.sol: Abstract v4 IHooks implementation (`CanonicalMarketCallback`) that authenticates PoolManager calls, decodes and authenticates a fixed-format 128-byte hookData payload (`CanonicalSwapHookData`, domain-separated by `HOOKEMON_CANONICAL_SWAP_R54_A3_V1`), enforces canonical PoolKey matching (currency ordering, hook address, tickSpacing, zero LP/protocol fee live-read), implements the quadrant-dependent before/after swap fee-delta logic, requires full fill (reverts on any partial fill), and hands the executed USDG amount + pre-collection balance to the (abstract) accounting layer.
purpose.FeeAccounting.sol: Abstract internal USDG liability ledger. Splits executed USDG volume into programmable/treasury/process buckets on every authenticated swap, tracks per-beneficiary and per-payoutId claimable liabilities plus a running `totalLiabilityAmount`, gates all money-moving internal functions behind a `moneyPath` reentrancy flag, and enforces `_isSolvent()` (hook's real USDG balance >= sum of all liabilities) before and after every liability mutation and every token transfer.
purpose.RobinhoodBindings.sol: Pure library + two tiny contracts used to freeze and validate the exact Robinhood-chain deployment: chain id 4663, all known Robinhood provider addresses, the fee-contract constants (300/10/40 bps), canonical PoolKey/poolId derivation, CREATE2 hook-address preimage check, and three evidence digests (source/abi/runtime). `validateQuadrant`/`_validateHookAccounting` is an independent re-derivation of the same fee/quadrant math implemented in CanonicalMarket.sol, apparently meant for off-chain/deployment-time or test-time cross-checking (it is not imported by HookemonHook.sol or CanonicalMarket.sol themselves). `ImmutableLaunchBinding` is a small immutable-storage contract that freezes a validated Binding's digest and key addresses. `PermanentPositionCustody` is an ERC721 receiver that permanently custodies the LP position NFT minted by Robinhood's PositionManager and verifies real on-chain ownership before treating it as received.

invariants: Hook permission mask is hard-pinned to 0x00CC (beforeSwap+afterSwap+beforeSwapReturnDelta+afterSwapReturnDelta only) both by HookemonHook's own constructor self-check against the deployed address and by RobinhoodBindings.validate(); matches v4-core Hooks.sol flag bits exactly (BEFORE_SWAP=1<<7, AFTER_SWAP=1<<6, BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA=1<<3, AFTER_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA=1<<2 => 0x80+0x40+0x08+0x04=0xCC), verified against the pinned lib/v4-core/src/libraries/Hooks.sol.

Every swap callback checks msg.sender == address(poolManager) (ForeignPoolManager), and hookData's encoded sender must equal both the PoolManager-supplied `sender` argument and the immutable `swapRouter` -- swaps not routed through the one canonical router cannot receive hook treatment.

A single-flight state machine (Idle->Pending->Finalizing->Idle) plus a recomputed context hash (_context) ties one beforeSwap call to exactly one matching afterSwap call for the same sender/key/params/hookData, rejecting reentry (ReentrantCallback) and rejecting non-full-fill swaps (InvalidFinalizedSwap) -- **partial fills are forbidden outright** rather than fee-accounted at actual executed volume.

_matches() re-derives canonical currency ordering from immutable usdg/hkmn addresses, requires k.fee==0, k.tickSpacing==immutable tickSpacing, k.hooks==address(this), AND does a live StateLibrary.getSlot0 read requiring the pool's current protocolFee==0 and liveLpFee==0 -- a runtime guard against a governance-set nonzero protocol fee siphoning value outside the hook's accounting.

Total fee is a flat 3% (300 bps) of executed USDG volume, taken via poolManager.take() exactly once per swap either in beforeSwap (when USDG is the specified currency) or afterSwap (when it is not), matching the Programmable policy's quadrant table exactly for both currency0=usdg and currency1=usdg orientations (independently re-verified bit-for-bit against programmable-fee-policy.md's quadrant table).

_accrueAuthenticatedSwap requires balanceAfterCollection-balanceBeforeCollection == recomputed totalFee exactly (InvalidCollectionDelta), i.e. it independently re-derives the fee from executedUsdg rather than trusting the amount already taken, and requires post-state solvency (_isSolvent) after every liability credit and after every claim/debit.

moneyPath boolean reentrancy guard: every liability-mutating/token-moving internal function requires _requireEnteredMoneyPath(); HookemonHook.afterSwap (the only path that calls _collectFee/_accrueAuthenticatedSwap) is the sole external entry marked with the `moneyPath` modifier that sets the flag.

_transferUsdg/_usdgBalanceOf use raw low-level call/staticcall with the exact standard ERC20 selectors (transfer=0xa9059cbb, balanceOf=0x70a08231) and revert/return false on any malformed or failing return -- fail-closed as the file's own doc comment promises.

_transferExactUsdg additionally verifies exact balance deltas on both source and destination after the transfer call (TokenBalanceDeltaMismatch), guarding against unexpected fee-on-transfer/deflationary token behavior even though USDG is expected to be a plain ERC20.

RobinhoodBindings.validate() locks the deployment to chain id 4663, requirements revision 54, architecture revision 3, all 6 known Robinhood addresses, fee bps 300/10/40, canonical currency ordering + keccak256-derived poolId, CREATE2 hook-address preimage (hookDeployer/hookSalt/hookInitCodeHash), and three non-zero evidence digests.
stateTransitions: CallbackPhase: Idle -[beforeSwap, PoolManager, matching key+full nonzero amountSpecified+valid hookData]-> Pending -[afterSwap, same context hash, full-fill delta]-> Finalizing (fee collected + accrued here) -> Idle (context cleared) at end of afterSwap.

FeeAccounting liabilities: on _accrueAuthenticatedSwap, programmableLiabilities[fixedProgrammableBeneficiary] += programmableFee; treasuryLiabilities[currentTreasuryBeneficiary] += treasuryFee; processLiabilityAmount += processFee; totalLiabilityAmount += totalFee (all monotonic increases at accrual time).

Claim: liabilities[beneficiary] snapshotted to `amount`, zeroed, totalLiabilityAmount -= amount, USDG transferred, solvency re-checked before and after -- HookemonHook.claimProgrammable/claimTreasury use msg.sender as both the authorization subject and the actual liability key/transfer recipient (destination param is authorization-only, forced equal to the stored beneficiary by MoneyRoles._authorizeProgrammableClaim/_authorizeTreasuryClaim, which live in access/MoneyRoles.sol outside this file set).
buyerHkmnCredit[recipient] and totalBuyerHkmnCredit only ever increase, credited once per successful afterSwap where rawHkmnDelta>0 (i.e. the swap recipient received HKMN).

autonomyGaps: No minimum-swap-size / dust-swap revert exists anywhere in the kernel. The mandatory Programmable fee policy (programmable-fee-policy.md) requires 'a positive gross quote amount below 1,000 smallest quote-asset units must revert atomically' specifically to close a 'split-swap bypass' where many small swaps could each round the platform fee to zero. Neither CanonicalMarket.sol's _fee() nor FeeAccounting.sol's _splitLiability() implement this threshold; both simply floor per-swap with no revert, so an executedUsdg of 1-999 (USDG has 6 decimals, i.e. swaps below 0.001 USDG) pays literally zero total fee, and executedUsdg up to 999 pays zero Programmable fee specifically. For an autonomous system firing swaps every N minutes indefinitely, this is not immediately exploitable by the automation itself (its own pack-buy swaps will be far above 1000 units), but it means the deployed hook does not enforce a policy requirement that third-party swappers on the same pool could exploit to avoid the Programmable owner's entitlement -- a compliance gap the owner/reviewers should decide whether to accept or fix before Robinhood mainnet launch.

No cumulative-remainder mechanism exists. Policy 1.1.0 explicitly requires 'independent cumulative platform and project remainders for the lifetime of the canonical pool' so that splitting one large swap into many small ones cannot suppress the platform's total lifetime entitlement versus doing it as one swap. FeeAccounting._splitLiability recomputes and floors each of the 3 buckets independently PER SWAP with no carried fractional state; the test suite's own test_revision55RoundingAssignsEveryRemainderToProcess name shows this per-swap-floor-to-process design is deliberate (Phase-1/'revision 55' owner-approved), but it is a different guarantee than what the external Programmable policy mandates (which cares about the platform/Programmable bucket specifically, not just 'no fee lost overall'). This is the same root cause as the missing 1000-unit floor above and should be evaluated together.

The kernel enforces 'full fill or revert' (InvalidFinalizedSwap on any partial fill) rather than the fee-on-actual-executed-volume-after-partial-fill approach the mandatory policy's evidence item #4 describes. This eliminates any under/over-accounting risk from partial fills by construction, but for a fully autonomous 20-minute-cycle bot, any partial fill (e.g. thin early liquidity, a tight sqrtPriceLimitX96, or MEV-driven price movement between quote and execution) causes the entire swap to revert rather than partially execute -- with no retry/backoff logic visible in this file set (that would live in the not-yet-built dashboard/automation service).

claimProgrammable/claimTreasury both hard-require destination == the stored beneficiary itself (enforced in access/MoneyRoles.sol's _authorizeProgrammableClaim/_authorizeTreasuryClaim, which this unit calls but does not define). The Programmable policy explicitly asks for 'a destination selected by the owner for that claim' as a *capability* the owner may use; as currently wired the `destination` function parameter exists in the ABI but can never differ from the immutable owner address, so per-claim destination selection is not actually implemented (safe, but incomplete relative to the policy's stated capability).

No event is emitted when a liability is claimed (_claimLiability in FeeAccounting.sol has no `emit`). Only CanonicalSwapObserved fires on swap accrual; there is no ProgrammableClaimed/TreasuryClaimed-style event. Policy evidence item #13 expects 'collection and claim events reconcile exactly with balances and liabilities' -- an off-chain dashboard/status page (part of the owner's Phase-2 target) would have no on-chain event to index claims from with this kernel alone.

For the owner's fully-autonomous target, nothing in these 4 files performs or triggers the buy-pack / open-pack / sell-card / redistribute cycle -- this kernel is exactly and only the swap-fee accounting layer for the canonical USDG/HKMN pool. The process-budget liability bucket (_processLiability, _debitProcessLiability) is a bare ledger primitive with a comment 'the final role-gated money path must hold this component's lock around the complete token transfer' -- i.e. by this file's own admission, the actual authorized spend/settlement path for the 2.50% process budget is not implemented here (expected to live in process/ProcessBudget.sol and settlement/HolderSettlement.sol, outside this unit).

suspicions.note: _splitLiability(executedUsdg) floors each of the 3 fee buckets independently with no minimum-volume revert and no cumulative remainder carry-forward. Combined with CanonicalMarket.sol's _fee() (line 272) having the same gap, this means the mandatory Programmable fee policy's two anti-split-swap protections (revert below 1000 smallest quote units; independent cumulative platform/project remainders) are both absent. This is the most consequential single finding for policy compliance -- confirmed by grepping the whole non-lib repo for any related threshold/remainder language and finding none, so it does not appear to be a deliberate, documented exception.

_validateFinalizedSwap enforces full-fill-or-revert instead of fee-on-actual-executed-volume. This is a defensible simplification (it structurally satisfies 'basis = actual executed amount' by making executed always equal requested), but it directly forgoes the partial-fill support the policy's evidence item #4 calls for, and gives the autonomous 20-minute cycle a hard revert on any partial fill with no in-kernel fallback.

validate(Binding memory) checks 12 addresses are non-zero and pairwise-distinct and pins 5 of them (usdg, poolManager, positionManager, router, launcher) to the exact known Robinhood addresses, but never checks binding.programmableBeneficiary against the Programmable policy's mandated immutable owner address 0x4957f49620AFf3Adbbe8195a4f633E49cc93376c. A repo-wide grep (excluding lib/ and the read-only skill directory) found this address nowhere in the codebase. Nothing in these 4 files -- or apparently anywhere else in packages/contracts -- forces the deployed hook's Programmable beneficiary to be the policy-mandated owner; it is only ever a plain constructor/config parameter (HookemonHook.ConstructorConfig.programmable) whose correctness at deployment time is left entirely to whatever off-chain deployment script/binding data supplies it.

_claimProgrammableLiability()/_claimTreasuryLiability() key and pay out to msg.sender, not to the `beneficiary`/`destination` parameters threaded through HookemonHook.claimProgrammable/claimTreasury. This is NOT a fund-misdirection bug -- access/MoneyRoles.sol's _authorizeProgrammableClaim/_authorizeTreasuryClaim (outside this file set) independently force `beneficiary == storedBeneficiary`, `msg.sender == storedBeneficiary`, and `destination == storedBeneficiary` before this code runs -- but the `destination` argument is consequently dead/vestigial in the current wiring (always forced equal to the fixed beneficiary), which is worth a reviewer's explicit sign-off given the policy's language about owner-selectable claim destinations.

validateQuadrant/_validateHookAccounting is a complete, independent re-implementation of the same fee-split and quadrant-delta math already implemented in CanonicalMarket.sol/FeeAccounting.sol, but it is not imported or called by HookemonHook.sol or CanonicalMarket.sol in this file set (only referenced by test/bindings/*.t.sol per grep). Two independently-maintained copies of safety-critical fee math is a maintenance/drift risk even though the current two versions are mathematically equivalent (verified by hand: both compute floor(x*bps/10000) per bucket with process/project absorbing the remainder) -- a future edit to one copy's constants without the other would silently desynchronize an on-chain enforcement path from its off-chain/test verifier.

beforeInitialize/afterInitialize/beforeAddLiquidity/afterAddLiquidity/beforeRemoveLiquidity/afterRemoveLiquidity/beforeDonate/afterDonate are all gated `onlyPoolManager` and then unconditionally `revert UnusedHookCallback()`. Since the hook's mined permission-mask bits for all of these are off, PoolManager's own Hooks.sol dispatch logic should never call them at all (they're dead from PoolManager's perspective), so the onlyPoolManager gate here adds no real protection and only matters for a stray direct call from an arbitrary EOA/contract, which would revert anyway. Not a bug, just slightly redundant code worth a reviewer's note.
